title: Cottage cheese wrap
summary: Cottage cheese and two eggs blended smooth and baked into a flat sheet that rolls like a wrap. About 38 g of protein for 320 calories, before you put anything in it.

time.note: Plus 5 to 10 minutes cooling in the tray, which is when it sets enough to lift.

nutrition_per_serving.note: The wrap on its own, before fillings. Assumes low-fat cottage cheese and medium eggs; full-fat cottage cheese takes it to about 380 calories and 20 g of fat.

ingredients.note: The western kind, soft curds in a little whey. In India, packs labelled cottage cheese are often paneer, which does not melt into a sheet and will not work here.
What sets the cottage cheese into something you can lift and roll.
Go easy. The cottage cheese already carries about 2 g of salt before you add any.
What the video used. Any dry seasoning works - see the tips.

steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a tray or shallow tin with baking paper.
Blend the cottage cheese, eggs and seasoning until completely smooth. Whole curds bake into lumps, and the wrap tears wherever one sits.

Pour it into the lined tray and spread it into an even layer with the back of a spoon. Even, but not too thin: a thin layer bakes crisp all the way through and cracks when you roll it, and the soft middle is what lets it bend.
Bake 25 minutes, until the top is golden all over. The colour is the test, not the clock - a pale top means the inside is still too soft to lift.
Leave it in the tray for 5 to 10 minutes before peeling it off the paper. It firms up as it cools.
tips: Garlic and herb: 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp dried oregano and plenty of black pepper, all blended into the batter. Neutral enough for any filling.
Everything bagel: 1/2 tsp each of garlic and onion powder in the blend, then a tablespoon of sesame seeds scattered over the top before baking, so they toast and help the crust take colour.
Smoky taco: 1/2 tsp smoked paprika, 1/4 tsp cumin and a pinch of chilli flakes in the blend. Made for a burrito-style filling of chicken or beans.
Masala: 1/2 tsp garam masala, 1/4 tsp red chilli powder and a pinch of crushed kasuri methi in the blend. It turns the wrap into a paratha stand-in for paneer tikka or keema.
Keep the seasoning dry. Fresh herbs, onion or garlic bring water with them, and water is exactly what stops the top going golden.
No blender: mash the cottage cheese hard with a fork before beating in the eggs. It works, but expect a lumpier, more fragile sheet.
It keeps a couple of days in the fridge. Warm it in a dry pan rather than the microwave, which turns it rubbery.
health_notes: Cottage cheese is roughly 12 g of protein per 100 g, so the 225 g here carries about two thirds of the wrap's 38 g, with the eggs making up the rest. It is also a salty cheese, which is why the added salt is kept to a pinch.

source.title: This Really Shouldn't Work...
source.adapted: Ingredients, bake and cooling from the video description. Two method details come from the video itself: everything is blended rather than just mixed, and the batter is spread evenly but deliberately not thin. The description says any seasonings; the video used salt and garlic powder, which is what the ingredient list records. Nutrition holds against the stated 310 calories and 37 g protein only with low-fat cottage cheese and medium eggs - two large eggs alone are about 10.6 g of the 12 g of fat quoted.
